name: Hunter
summary: Across Azeroth, hunters follow wild trails with loyal beasts at their sides. Bows, rifles, and crossbows let them strike from afar, while traps and primal aspects help control a fight. They track quarry through forests and over snowbound peaks, relying on their wits and bond with nature.

sections.title: Kinship with the Wild
sections.body: Hunters make their lives among Azeroth’s wild places. They study how beasts move, hunt, and defend themselves, earning respect instead of breaking spirits. With patience, they can tame dangerous creatures, from prowling cats to mountain bears and sharp-eyed raptors. These animals become steadfast allies, ready to defend their companions to the death.

sections.title: Master Marksmen and Trackers
sections.body: Hunters fight from a distance with bows, heavy crossbows, and rifles. Their volleys can pierce heavy armor before an attacker draws near. Keen senses lead them along faint footsteps, scents, and other signs left by their quarry. When enemies close in, frost and flame traps, disorienting ambushes, and quick evasive movements keep foes at bay.

sections.title: Traditions Across Cultures
sections.body:
The hunter’s path takes many forms across Azeroth. Night elf Sentinels use bows and shadowcraft beneath Ashenvale’s canopy, moving in quiet accord with the wilderness. Dwarven riflemen brave Dun Morogh’s freezing crags with hardy bears and master the craft of gunpowder. Across Kalimdor, Tauren and Orc trackers follow ancient nomadic customs. They pursue prey with sacred respect and call on bestial spirits to guide their shots.

In Elwynn Forest, young humans learn from seasoned trackers such as the dwarf Tordrin Sternblade in Northshire Valley and Josephine Carson in Goldshire. The Skyborne learn to track and tame the beasts of Zephras Isle.

faq.answer: Hunters fight with ranged weapons such as bows, crossbows, and rifles. At close quarters, they also wield polearms, staves, axes, and daggers. Traps make room for them to shoot again.
Hunters study wild creatures and approach them without malice. By showing strength and respect, they can soothe dangerous predators and form a lasting bond, training a beast to fight at their side.
Hunters begin in light leather armor, which lets them move freely over rugged ground. With experience, they learn to wear sturdy mail for greater protection without greatly hindering their movement.
A hunter’s aspects attune the senses and body to strengths found in wild creatures. One can bring the fleetness of a cheetah, the keen focus of a hawk, or the resilience of a monkey.

faq.q: What happens if an enemy gets too close to a hunter?
faq.answer: At close range, hunters struggle to fire their ranged weapons. Frost and immolation traps, concussive tools, and melee strikes can slow, wound, or disorient an attacker while the hunter or their beast retreats to regain distance.

faq.q: Which races practice the ways of the hunter?
faq.answer: Many peoples practice the hunt in their own ways. Night elves, dwarves, and humans in the Alliance favor bows and rifles; orcs, tauren, and trolls in the Horde honor tracking and beast mastery as ancestral ways of survival. The Skyborne train hunters on both sides, while gnomes and the Forsaken do not follow the hunter’s path.

angles.text: Your bond with the wild and your companion beast are your strengths. Master your ranged weapons, keep your distance, and let your beast hold the enemy’s attention.
For millennia, Kaldorei Sentinels have patrolled ancient forests with bows and trusted sabers, guarding sacred groves from outside corruption.
Dwarven marksmen are known for their skill with heavy rifles. They brave Khaz Modan’s treacherous mountain passes alongside fierce polar bears.
To the Tauren, the hunt is a sacred trial of endurance and reverence. They honor the Earth Mother by respecting every beast that feeds and clothes the tribe.
Orcish beastmasters keep ancestral survival traditions forged on harsh worlds. They form strong combat bonds with loyal wolves and boars.
In Elwynn Forest, human hunters learn from seasoned trackers such as the dwarf Tordrin Sternblade in Northshire Valley and Josephine Carson in Goldshire.
Skyborne hunters learn to track and tame the beasts of Zephras Isle, a floating land adrift in Skywall.
